title: Life-cycle funds and the glide path
intro: India's first target-date funds: pick the year, and the fund gets more careful as it approaches.

steps.title: One fund, one year
steps.body:
A life-cycle fund is an open-end scheme built around a **single target year in its name** — 2031, 2036, 2041, 2046, 2051. You pick the year closest to when you'll need the money; the fund handles allocation, rebalancing, and the gradual **equity → debt** shift as the year nears.

The logic: far from the goal you can carry risk (time absorbs swings); near it, capital preservation wins — an all-equity corpus the year before retirement is exposure at the worst possible moment.

steps.title: Feel it — the machine
steps.body: Run the glide, then crash the market early and again near the target. Same crash, wildly different cost — the de-risking *is* the product:

viz.title: The glide path, live
viz.caption: Each second is a year. The crash button cuts the equity sleeve 30% — watch its cost shrink as the glide de-risks.

steps.title: SEBI's rulebook
steps.body:
- **Glide-path bands** the manager must stay within (ranges — two same-year funds can differ).
- Non-core (gold/silver ETFs, InvITs, ETCDs) capped at **10% combined**.
- Max **six schemes** per fund house; near maturity, debt limited to **AA+ maturing before target**; merge-on-maturity with consent.
- **Graded exit loads** (3/2/1% over three years) instead of a lock-in; TER capped at **2.1%**.

steps.title: Context and contrast
steps.body:
US target-date funds hold ~**$4.8 trillion** as the workplace default (auto-enrolled since 2006). India's **NPS** has offered a glide for years — but locks Tier I money 15 years / to age 60, rewarding patience with a tax break. A life-cycle fund is the **open wrapper**: any dated goal, redeemable after the exit-load window. Different jobs; they can sit side by side.

> [!tip] The category launched **passive-first** (Zerodha; ICICI's active filings follow) — a milestone for index investing in India, and an open question of what active management adds inside fixed bands.

recap:
**Pick the year; the glide handles the rest.**

- Equity → debt automatically as the target approaches; late crashes hurt less.
- Rules: banded glides, 10% non-core cap, 6 schemes, 3/2/1% exit loads, 2.1% TER cap.
- NPS = locked, tax-advantaged retirement glide; life-cycle = open wrapper for any dated goal.
- Same year ≠ same path — check the glide within the bands.
